---
title: "Learning Path"
---

## From information exposure to epistemic agency

DSA261 is organised as a progression rather than a list of disconnected AI topics.

The course develops through four phases:

> **Know → Understand → Use → Govern**

TRACE provides the recurring working method:

> **Predict → Encounter → Probe → Explain → Decide → Verify**

---

## Phase I — Know, Search, Question

**Weeks 1–3**

The first phase develops information literacy and epistemic discipline before moving deeper into AI systems.

- [Week 1 — How Do You Know?](weeks/week01.qmd)  
  Information seeking, source tracing, verification, and confidence calibration.

- [Week 2 — Who Decides What You See?](weeks/week02.qmd)  
  Ranking, recommendation, targeting, computational propaganda, and the distinction between exposure and effect.

- [Week 3 — Is This AI?](weeks/week03.qmd)  
  Automation, machine learning, predictive AI, generative AI, and AI claim auditing.

---

## Phase II — Understand and Stress-Test AI

**Weeks 4–6**

The second phase moves from identifying AI systems to understanding and testing their behaviour.

- [Week 4 — What Does an LLM Actually Do?](weeks/week04.qmd)  
  Tokens, prediction, attention, context, generation, retrieval, and controlled variation.

- [Week 5 — Can AI Make You Better?](weeks/week05.qmd)  
  Capability boundaries, benchmark interpretation, skill boosting, and verification cost.

- [Week 6 — When Algorithms Decide About People](weeks/week06.qmd)  
  Risk scores, false positives, false negatives, fairness metrics, and counterfactual probing.

---

## Week 7 — TRACE Midterm Challenge

The midterm integrates the first six weeks into one reconstructable investigation.

- [Week 7 — TRACE Midterm Challenge](weeks/week07.qmd)

The assessment focuses on:

- provenance;
- search and interaction trails;
- meaningful probes;
- evidence quality;
- verification;
- inference discipline;
- human judgment;
- transparent AI use.

---

## Phase III — Use, Control, Verify

**Weeks 8–11**

The third phase develops increasingly deliberate control over LLM-assisted work.

- [Week 8 — Prompt Design Studio](weeks/week08.qmd)  
  Task specification, context, constraints, evidence requirements, and iterative prompting.

- [Week 9 — Context Drift](weeks/week09.qmd)  
  Context-window capacity, context utilisation, irrelevant and conflicting context, and strategic resets.

- [Week 10 — Hallucination Hunt](weeks/week10.qmd)  
  Fabricated citations, unsupported claims, source distortion, and independent verification.

- [Week 11 — Academic Integrity and AI-Use Judgment](weeks/week11.qmd)  
  AI-use boundaries, assessment validity, disclosure, and the Use–Modify–Disclose–Reject framework.

---

## Phase IV — Govern and Transfer

**Weeks 12–14**

The final phase shifts from competent use toward governance, accountability, and transfer.

- [Week 12 — Context-Specific AI Guidelines](weeks/week12.qmd)  
  Risk profiles, professional rules, verification thresholds, and Final Project Gate 1.

- [Week 13 — Professional Accountability and Design Freeze](weeks/week13.qmd)  
  Human oversight, automation bias, decision rights, stop conditions, and Final Project Gate 2.

- [Week 14 — TRACE Transfer and Final Readiness](weeks/week14.qmd)  
  Transfer to unfamiliar problems, evidence auditing, and final readiness.

---

## Final Project

The course concludes with three authentic discipline-specific tasks and a comparative analysis of AI-assisted work.

- [Open the TRACE Final Project](final-project.qmd)

The Final Project asks you to demonstrate:

- effective task specification;
- meaningful probing;
- context control;
- independent verification;
- documented failure or limitation;
- explicit human judgment;
- transfer across different tasks;
- a Personal AI/LLM Use Charter.

---

## Skills you are building

`SEEK` · `PROMPT` · `PROBE` · `CONTEXT` · `VERIFY` · `JUDGE` · `TRANSFER`

These capacities accumulate across the course rather than belonging to only one week.
